chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Burayd al-Ajli from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who has a female slave (concubine) and he divorces her with two divorces, then later buys her back: He said, 'It is not permissible for him to marry her until she marries another husband, until she enters into the same state from which she exited.'

key_terms.تَدْخُلَ فِي مِثْلِ مَا خَرَجَتْ مِنْهُ: Enters into the same state from which she exited

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his female slave with two divorces and then buys her back?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific application of the 'two divorces' rule to slave women, requiring a full consummation and separation with a third party before the original owner can remarry her, mirroring the general rule for free women. It highlights the juristic nuance in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* regarding the transition of status for concubines, ensuring the bond is fully severed before re-establishment.
